question: A digital catch certificate system, known as CATCH, for all fishery products entering the EU came into force on 10 January 2026. The ambitious system replaced the previous paper-based process and is considered central to EU efforts to tackle illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, help protect marine biodiversity and contribute to the EU’s broader efforts to simplify administrative procedures. 1.
How much did the CATCH system cost to develop?

What was this money spent on (e.g. consultation and planning, information infrastructure, programming or testing)? The Commission is asked to itemise the amounts over the entire period of development.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) 1. The total cost of CATCH development amounts to approximately EUR 2 750 000. 2. There were two main phases of CATCH development. The first one (2016 - 2019) included feasibility study, inception, prototyping and building of the first version that was deployed in 2019.

The second one (2020 - 2025) included operation and maintenance of the first version and building of a new version to align the system with the updated legal requirements of the amended Council Regulation (EC) 1005/20081. The costs incurred in the first and the second phase were approximately EUR 800 000 and EUR 1 950 000, respectively.

A more detailed breakdown of the total cost is as follows: analysis and study: EUR 1 000 000; development: EUR 1 450 000; helpdesk, hosting, user documentation and overhead: EUR 300 000. The hosting cost is kept low thanks to the synergies obtained by building CATCH as a module in TRACES NT2 platform and applying the ‘reuse’ principle for several functionalities already available in that platform.

Beyond a digitalisation effort, CATCH is the first-ever EU-wide real-time system to harmonise and strengthen controls of fisheries imports across the EU, and indeed the first of its kind globally. As such, it also provides for a level-playing field between EU and non-EU fisheries.

Since its start on 10 January 2026, more than 115 000 importer declarations have been validated in CATCH by Member States, showing that the system is operational. Moreover, CATCH has already proved itself as a game changer, with third country exports of fish stemming from illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing being identified and blocked by Member States’ authorities.
